hints: Count all strings and subtract those that never complete the required pattern.
Track the longest suffix of the current string that is also a prefix of the pattern.
Build KMP prefix-function transitions and use dynamic programming over length and matched-prefix length.
analogy: A progress marker on the pattern moves forward on matching letters and falls back to a shorter matching prefix on a mismatch.
example: For length 2 and required pattern AB over uppercase letters, only AB works, so the answer is 1.
algorithm: Build transitions for each proper prefix length and each of the 26 letters using the prefix function. Start with one empty string at state zero. For each of n positions, extend each state by every letter; when a transition completes the pattern, count it as already successful, or equivalently count only avoiding strings and subtract their total from 26^n. Work modulo 10^9+7.
correctness: The state is exactly the longest pattern prefix that is a suffix, so it contains all information needed for the next character. The DP counts every avoiding string once; its complement is exactly the strings containing the pattern.
complexity: For pattern length m and target length n, O(26(nm+m)) time and O(m) DP space, plus O(26m) transitions.
